title: Tool crosswalk fallback runtime: tolerant name resolution & signature reconciliation
creator: Ava Singh
description: Problem: Customers and internal SDKs send invocation requests using a mix of OpenAI-style 'tool' metadata and older 'legacy function' payloads. Name collisions, parameter shape mismatches, streaming boundaries, and differing error semantics cause failed calls, incorrect telemetry, and poor fallbacks. This ticket proposes a lightweight runtime 'crosswalk' shim that sits in the invocation path to (1) resolve ambiguous names, (2) reconcile argument/return schemas with tolerant marshalling, (3) map streaming boundaries and finalization semantics, and (4) attach provenance/telemetry to enable safe rollouts.
context: Recent incidents: See incident dash INC-2025-014 (high rate of failed tool calls when customers upgraded SDKs). Telemetry shows ~2.3% of calls hit name collisions or schema errors last 30d. Existing solutions (alias registry, heuristic normalizer) live in separate repos and are brittle for streaming tool calls. We need a single runtime layer to avoid scattering fixes across SDKs, gateway, and runtime code.
goals: Reduce tool-invocation failures due to name/signature mismatches by >= 90% for mixed-protocol callers
Preserve streaming semantics: no additional end-to-end latency > 10ms p50 introduced by shim
Emit structured provenance and reason codes for every fallback/translation decision
Support gradual rollout and canarying per-customer and per-route
non_goals: Full reimplementation of legacy function runtimes (we only translate and route)
Replacing SDK-level validation (we complement, not remove it)
design_overview: The crosswalk runtime is an invocation middleware component deployed in the serving edge. On request: 1) Fast name resolution: consult local alias table, apply lightweight fuzzy heuristics (strip punctuation, normalize camel/snake, known synonyms). 2) Signature reconciliation: use best-effort marshalling rules (coerce types when safe, accept extra/unknown fields as opaque metadata, map positional<->named args) with user-visible reason codes. 3) Streaming alignment: if caller requested chunked/streaming but target is legacy sync function, the shim buffers up to a small threshold and then calls; conversely, if target sends chunked events, the shim materializes them into the expected streaming frame format. 4) Fallback policy: configurable chain (preferred tool variant -> compatible model function -> legacy function -> error) with weights and timeouts. 5) Telemetry: annotate invocation with resolution path, translation diffs, and confidence score.
acceptance_criteria: Automated e2e tests with 30+ synthetic permutations show >= 90% successful resolution versus baseline
Latency regression test: p50 added by shim < 10ms, p95 < 50ms in 95% of test runs
Observability: crosswalk emits reason_code and resolution_path fields in invocation traces and logs
Runtime feature flagging and per-customer policy config exist and are controllable via console
Security review completed and no new injection vectors introduced by marshalling rules

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager coercion can change semantics -> Mitigation: conservative default rules; explicit opt-in permissive mode
Risk: Increased attack surface for injection via flexible marshalling -> Mitigation: sanitize and validate critical fields; enforce schema allowlists for privileged routes
Risk: Buffering for streaming->sync can increase latency -> Mitigation: small buffer thresholds, backpressure signalling, per-route config
Risk: Alias table drift -> Mitigation: TTL-based cache plus background reconciliation and a manual override UI
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood on staging for 2 weeks (10% of internal traffic). 2) Canary with 3 pilot customers with known mixed-protocol usage for 4 weeks. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of routes with monitoring alarms on failure rate, latency, and translation volume. 4) Full rollout gated on metrics and security sign-off.
telemetry_and_alerting: New metrics: crosswalk.resolutions.total, crosswalk.resolutions.failure, crosswalk.translations.per_reason, crosswalk.latency_ms.*. Alerts: translation-failure-rate > 0.5% for 1h, p95 latency regression > 2x baseline. Dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/TOOLS/crosswalk-overview

notes: This ticket intentionally keeps translation rules conservative. If a caller opts into permissive mode (via request header X-Redwood-Permissive-Interop: true), the crosswalk will apply additional fuzzy rules and best-effort conversions but will include explicit warning reason_codes in the response. Keep the permissive mode disabled for enterprise/high-security customers by default.
